354|    def fillet(self, edges="vertical", r=None):
355|        """Round the stock's 4 vertical outer edges; r defaults to the material standard."""
356|        self._guard_open("fillet()")

369|    def wall_hole(self, edge, code, at):
370|        """Plain KF clearance hole drilled horizontally through the wall on `edge`.
371|
372|        `u` = distance along the wall (from the west end for north/south walls,
373|        from the south end for east/west walls); `z` = hole-centre height above
374|        the stock top. Add the wall before its wall holes.
375|        """
376|        self._guard_open("wall_hole()")
377|        self._need_stock("wall_hole()")
378|        if edge not in _EDGES:
379|            raise KeelError(
380|                f"keel: unknown edge {edge!r}; edges are named "
381|                "'north', 'south', 'east' or 'west'"
382|            )

388|                "walls are too thin for counterbores or countersinks"

394|                    f"keel: wall_hole() {name} must be a number of millimetres, got {value!r}"
395|                )

397|        op = ("wall_hole", {"edge": edge, "code": code, "at": (float(u), float(z))})
398|        self._ops.append(op)

402|    def _walls_on(self, edge):
403|        return [p for kind, p in self._ops if kind == "wall" and p["edge"] == edge]

405|    def _check_wall_hole_fit(self, edge, code, u, z):
406|        walls = self._walls_on(edge)

408|            raise KeelError(
409|                f"keel: wall_hole() on the {edge!r} edge with no wall; "
410|                f"add p.wall({edge!r}, ...) first"
411|            )
412|        clr, _cb = KF[_split_code(code)[0]]
413|        r = clr / 2
414|        h = max(w["h"] for w in walls)
415|        L, W, _ = self._stock
416|        length = L if edge in ("north", "south") else W
417|        if u - r < 0 or u + r > length or z - r < 0 or z + r > h:
418|            raise KeelError(
419|                f"keel: wall_hole() {code} at (u={u:g}, z={z:g}) does not fit "
420|                f"the {edge} wall ({length:g} long, {h:g} high, hole dia {clr:g}); "
421|                "the hole edge must stay inside the wall face"
422|            )

424|    def mount(self, name, origin, finish="plain"):

427|        `finish` = "plain", "CB" or "CS", applied to every hole of the mount.
428|        Counts as one feature for pattern() and mirror(). On FLIGHT parts a
429|        "plain" mount raises KeelError, like a plain hole().
430|        """
431|        self._guard_open("mount()")
432|        self._need_stock("mount()")
433|        if finish not in ("plain", "CB", "CS"):
434|            raise KeelError(
435|                f"keel: unknown mount finish {finish!r}; finish is 'plain', 'CB' or 'CS'"
436|            )
437|        holes = _mount_holes(name, origin)  # also rejects unknown mount names
438|        (ox, oy) = origin
439|        for code, (hx, hy) in holes:
440|            eff = code if finish == "plain" else f"{code}-{finish}"

443|                raise self._flight_hole_error(code, hx, hy)
444|        op = {"name": name, "origin": (float(ox), float(oy)), "finish": finish}
445|        op = ("mount", op)
446|        self._ops.append(op)
447|        self._seed = op
448|        return self

450|    def mirror(self, axis):
451|        """Copy every hole, boss, pocket, slot and mount recorded so far.
452|
453|        axis="ew" mirrors about the stock centre line x = L/2; axis="ns"
454|        about y = W/2. Originals stay; walls and wall holes are not mirrored.
455|        After a mirror, pattern() raises KeelError.
456|        """
457|        self._guard_open("mirror()")
458|        self._need_stock("mirror()")
459|        if axis not in ("ew", "ns"):
460|            raise KeelError(
461|                f"keel: unknown mirror axis {axis!r}; axis is 'ew' (about x = L/2) "
462|                "or 'ns' (about y = W/2)"
463|            )
464|        L, W, _ = self._stock
465|        copies = []
466|        for kind, p in list(self._ops):

468|                x, y = p["at"]
469|                at = (L - x, y) if axis == "ew" else (x, W - y)
470|                copies.append(("hole", {"code": p["code"], "at": at}))
471|            elif kind == "boss":
472|                x, y = p["at"]
473|                at = (L - x, y) if axis == "ew" else (x, W - y)
474|                copies.append(("boss", {"at": at, "dia": p["dia"], "h": p["h"]}))
475|            elif kind == "pocket":
476|                x, y = p["at"]
477|                if axis == "ew":
478|                    at = (L - x - p["L"], y)
479|                else:
480|                    at = (x, W - y - p["W"])
481|                copies.append(("pocket", {"at": at, "L": p["L"], "W": p["W"],
482|                                          "depth": p["depth"]}))
483|            elif kind == "slot":
484|                (x1, y1), (x2, y2) = p["at"], p["to"]
485|                if axis == "ew":
486|                    at, to = (L - x1, y1), (L - x2, y2)
487|                else:

489|                copies.append(("slot", {"at": at, "to": to, "width": p["width"],
490|                                        "depth": p["depth"]}))
491|            elif kind == "mount":
492|                # Mirror the whole mount hole by hole; the mirrored set is what

496|                    at = (L - hx, hy) if axis == "ew" else (hx, W - hy)
497|                    copies.append(("hole", {"code": eff, "at": at}))

62|clearance Ø, then the through hole. "Local top" is the highest added material
63|covering the hole position (a wall or boss top if the hole sits on one, else
64|the stock top) — the same rule counterbores use.
65|
66|## 3. API
67|
68|```python
69|import keel
70|p = keel.part("BRK-0412", material="AL6061", cls="GSE")
71|```
72|
73|`cls` is `"GSE"` (default) or `"FLIGHT"`. FLIGHT rules: (1) `finish()` applies
74|your material's standard fillet to the stock's vertical edges automatically if
75|you never called `fillet()` (an explicit `fillet(r=...)` wins); (2) every base
76|hole must be `-CB` or `-CS` — a plain code raises
77|`keel: flight parts need -CB or -CS fasteners (KF-M4 at (6, 6))`. Wall holes
78|are exempt (they are always plain).
79|
80|**stock(L, W, T)** — the base block, x in [0, L], y in [0, W], z in [0, T].
81|Exactly one per part, and it must be the first call.
82|
83|```python
84|p.stock(60, 40, 4)
85|```
86|
87|**wall(edge, h, t=None)** — a wall standing on the top face along a named
88|edge (`north`, `south`, `east`, `west`). It sits flush with that edge, runs the
89|full edge length, and rises `h` above the stock top. `t` defaults to your
90|material's standard wall, and must not be below its minimum wall.
91|
92|```python
93|p.wall("north", 25)
94|```
95|
96|**boss(at=(x, y), dia, h)** — a cylinder on the top face centred at (x, y),
97|`h` high.
98|
99|```python
100|p.boss(at=(15, 15), dia=12, h=10)
101|```
102|
103|**hole(code, at=(x, y))** — a through hole, all the way down, using a KF code.
104|`-CB` adds the counterbore, `-CS` the countersink, both from the local top.
105|
106|```python
107|p.hole("KF-M4-CB", at=(8, 8))
108|```
109|
110|**wall_hole(edge, code, at=(u, z))** — a plain KF clearance hole drilled
111|horizontally through the wall on `edge`, perpendicular to the wall, all the way
112|through its thickness. `u` is the distance along the wall: from the **west
113|end** for north/south walls, from the **south end** for east/west walls. `z` is
114|the hole-centre height **above the stock top**. Add the wall before its wall
115|holes. It is a KeelError if there is no wall on that edge, if the code has
116|`-CB`/`-CS`, or if the hole edge leaves the wall face.
117|
118|```python
119|p.wall("north", 25)
120|p.wall_hole("north", "KF-M3", at=(30, 12))
121|```
122|
123|**mount(name, origin=(x, y), finish="plain")** — a company standard mount: a
124|fixed group of base holes. `finish` is `"plain"`, `"CB"` or `"CS"`, applied to
125|every hole of the mount (FLIGHT rule 2 applies). Offsets are from `origin`:
126|
127|| Name | Fastener | Holes (offsets from origin) |
128||------|----------|-----------------------------|
129|| PETREL-MOUNT-A | KF-M4 | (0,0), (40,0), (0,30), (40,30); origin = south-west hole |
130|| PETREL-MOUNT-B | KF-M5 | (0,0), (60,0), (0,40), (60,40); origin = south-west hole |
131|| STAR-TRACKER-3 | KF-M3 | 3 holes on a circle of diameter 30 about the origin, at 90°, 210°, 330° (0° = east, counter-clockwise) |
132|| HARNESS-P2 | KF-M2 | (0,0), (15,0); origin = west hole |
133|
134|A mount counts as one feature for `pattern()` (the whole mount is repeated)
135|and for `mirror()`.
136|
137|```python
138|p.mount("PETREL-MOUNT-A", origin=(10, 10), finish="CS")
139|```
140|
141|**pocket(at=(x, y), L, W, depth)** — a rectangular pocket cut from the top
142|face. (x, y) is the pocket's lower-left corner; `depth` must be less than the
143|stock thickness.
144|
145|```python
146|p.pocket(at=(10, 10), L=80, W=60, depth=4)
147|```
148|
149|**slot(at=(x1, y1), to=(x2, y2), width, depth="thru")** — a straight slot with
150|round ends along the centre line from start to end. `depth="thru"` cuts all the
151|way through; a number cuts a blind slot that deep from the top face.
152|
153|```python
154|p.slot(at=(10, 15), to=(40, 15), width=5)
155|```
156|
157|**pattern(nx, ny, dx, dy)** — repeats the LAST feature call in a grid, `nx`
158|by `ny` positions spaced `dx`, `dy` apart. The total is nx × ny instances
159|including the original call's position. Only boss, hole, pocket, slot and
160|mount can be patterned (a mount seed repeats the whole mount). After a
161|`mirror()`, `pattern()` raises a KeelError — there is nothing left to repeat.
162|(A leading text label, e.g. `pattern("hole", 2, 2, 48, 28)`, is accepted and
163|ignored.)
164|
165|```python
166|p.hole("KF-M4", at=(6, 6))
167|p.pattern(2, 2, 48, 28)
168|```
169|
170|**mirror(axis)** — copies every hole, boss, pocket, slot and mount recorded so
171|far to the mirror position: `axis="ew"` about the stock centre line x = L/2,
172|`axis="ns"` about y = W/2. Originals stay. Walls and wall holes are not
173|mirrored.
174|
175|```python
176|p.hole("KF-M5", at=(5, 5))
177|p.mirror("ew")   # second hole appears at (L-5, 5)
178|```
179|
180|**fillet(edges="vertical", r=None)** — rounds the stock's 4 vertical outer
181|edges. `r` defaults to your material's standard fillet. Only `edges="vertical"`
182|exists.
183|
184|```python
185|p.fillet()
186|```
187|
188|**finish()** — returns the part as exactly one solid. Must be the last call;
189|every program ends with `solid = p.finish()`.
190|
191|```python
192|solid = p.finish()
193|```
194|
195|**keel.render(p, path)** — writes an SVG preview of a finished part for the
196|dashboard catalogue. It needs a finished part, so call it after `finish()`.
197|
198|```python
199|keel.render(p, "brk_0101.svg")
200|```

202|## 4. Error messages
203|
204|Keel errors are plain sentences starting with `keel:`. The common ones:
205|
206|- `keel: unknown fastener code 'M4'; holes use company codes KF-M2 ...` — you
207|  used a raw size instead of a KF code.
208|- `keel: stock() called twice; a part has exactly one base block ...` — delete
209|  the second `stock()`.
210|- `keel: hole() called before stock(); every part starts with p.stock(L, W, T)`
211|  — `stock()` must be the first call.
212|- `keel: unknown edge 'top'; edges are named 'north', 'south', 'east' or 'west'`.
213|- `keel: pattern() with no previous feature; call a feature first`.
214|- `keel: render() before p.finish(); finish the part first ...`.
215|- `keel: unknown material 'AL7075'; materials are AL6061, TI6AL4V, SS316 ...`.
216|- `keel: wall thickness 1.0 is thinner than the AL6061 minimum wall 1.5 ...`.
217|- `keel: flight parts need -CB or -CS fasteners (KF-M4 at (6, 6))` — FLIGHT
218|  parts need counterbored or countersunk base holes.
219|- `keel: wall_hole() on the 'north' edge with no wall; ...` — add the wall first.
220|- `keel: wall_hole() takes a plain KF code without -CB/-CS, got ...`.
221|- `keel: unknown mount 'PETREL-MOUNT-C'; mounts are ...`.
222|- `keel: pattern() after mirror(); there is nothing to repeat ...`.

1|# Keel manual (internal wiki)
2|
3|*Quillon Orbital Works · Structures team · Keel v2.0.0 · QX-2 controlled: on-prem only.*
4|*Fictional company, made for the Forge demo.*
5|
6|Keel is our small internal tool for describing machined satellite parts in Python.
7|A Keel program is a short recipe: start from a base block, add walls and bosses,
8|cut holes, pockets and slots, and finish with exactly one solid. Keel compiles
9|the recipe to a solid model internally, and the Gauge station checks the result
10|against the design request. If you can write the recipe, you can make the part.
11|
12|v2 adds company knowledge: materials that change the standards, flight-part
13|rules, countersinks, holes in walls, standard mounts, and mirroring. Every v1
14|program still builds exactly the same solid.
15|
16|## 1. Conventions (read this first)
17|
18|All dimensions are millimetres. The datum is the part's **lower-left-bottom
19|corner** at (0, 0, 0): +X points east, +Y points north, +Z points up. Nothing is
20|centred unless the call says so; every position is measured from the datum.
21|Exception: **FRM requests are dimensioned from the frame centre** (section 6).
22|
23|The four edges of the base stock have names: **north** (+Y side), **south**
24|(−Y side), **east** (+X side), **west** (−X side).
25|
26|Holes never use raw diameters. Always use a **company fastener code** from
27|table KF below; the Gauge station checks the exact diameters, so a 4 mm drill
28|where a KF-M4 belongs will FAIL the part.
29|
30|Standards depend on the material (section 2). Whenever a request says
31|"standard", use your material's row. "Flight part" in a request means
32|`cls="FLIGHT"` (section 3).
33|
34|Part numbers tell you the family: BRK (bracket), PLT (plate), FRM (frame),
35|STD (standoff), CLP (clip).
36|
37|A program has a fixed shape: one `stock()` call first, then features, then
38|`p.finish()` last. `finish()` returns the single solid.
39|
40|## 2. Materials and fastener table KF
41|
42|| Material | Standard wall | Standard fillet | Minimum wall |
43||----------|---------------|-----------------|--------------|
44|| AL6061 (aluminium) | 2.5 | 1.0 | 1.5 |
45|| TI6AL4V (titanium) | 3.0 | 1.5 | 2.0 |
46|| SS316 (stainless) | 2.0 | 0.5 | 1.2 |
47|
48|A wall thinner than your material's minimum is rejected with a KeelError.
49|An unknown material is rejected; the three codes above are the only ones.
50|
51|| Code  | Clearance hole Ø | Counterbore Ø × depth | Countersink Ø at top |
52||-------|------------------|-----------------------|-----------------------|
53|| KF-M2 | 2.4              | 4.4 × 2.0             | 4.3                   |
54|| KF-M3 | 3.4              | 6.5 × 3.0             | 6.3                   |
55|| KF-M4 | 4.5              | 8.0 × 4.0             | 8.4                   |
56|| KF-M5 | 5.5              | 10.0 × 5.0            | 10.4                  |
57|| KF-M6 | 6.6              | 11.0 × 6.0            | 12.4                  |
58|
59|Suffix `-CB` means counterbored from the local top face, e.g. `KF-M4-CB`.
60|Suffix `-CS` means a 90° countersink from the local top face, e.g. `KF-M4-CS`:
61|a cone from the countersink Ø at the local top narrowing at 45° down to the
62|clearance Ø, then the through hole. "Local top" is the highest added material
63|covering the hole position (a wall or boss top if the hole sits on one, else
64|the stock top) — the same rule counterbores use.
65|
66|## 3. API
67|
68|```python
69|import keel
70|p = keel.part("BRK-0412", material="AL6061", cls="GSE")
71|```
72|
73|`cls` is `"GSE"` (default) or `"FLIGHT"`. FLIGHT rules: (1) `finish()` applies
74|your material's standard fillet to the stock's vertical edges automatically if
75|you never called `fillet()` (an explicit `fillet(r=...)` wins); (2) every base
76|hole must be `-CB` or `-CS` — a plain code raises
77|`keel: flight parts need -CB or -CS fasteners (KF-M4 at (6, 6))`. Wall holes
78|are exempt (they are always plain).
79|
80|**stock(L, W, T)** — the base block, x in [0, L], y in [0, W], z in [0, T].
81|Exactly one per part, and it must be the first call.
82|
83|```python
84|p.stock(60, 40, 4)
85|```
86|
87|**wall(edge, h, t=None)** — a wall standing on the top face along a named
88|edge (`north`, `south`, `east`, `west`). It sits flush with that edge, runs the
89|full edge length, and rises `h` above the stock top. `t` defaults to your
90|material's standard wall, and must not be below its minimum wall.
91|
92|```python
93|p.wall("north", 25)
94|```
95|
96|**boss(at=(x, y), dia, h)** — a cylinder on the top face centred at (x, y),
97|`h` high.
98|
99|```python
100|p.boss(at=(15, 15), dia=12, h=10)
101|```
102|
103|**hole(code, at=(x, y))** — a through hole, all the way down, using a KF code.
104|`-CB` adds the counterbore, `-CS` the countersink, both from the local top.
105|
106|```python
107|p.hole("KF-M4-CB", at=(8, 8))
108|```
109|
110|**wall_hole(edge, code, at=(u, z))** — a plain KF clearance hole drilled
111|horizontally through the wall on `edge`, perpendicular to the wall, all the way
112|through its thickness. `u` is the distance along the wall: from the **west
113|end** for north/south walls, from the **south end** for east/west walls. `z` is
114|the hole-centre height **above the stock top**. Add the wall before its wall
115|holes. It is a KeelError if there is no wall on that edge, if the code has
116|`-CB`/`-CS`, or if the hole edge leaves the wall face.
117|
118|```python
119|p.wall("north", 25)
120|p.wall_hole("north", "KF-M3", at=(30, 12))
121|```
122|
123|**mount(name, origin=(x, y), finish="plain")** — a company standard mount: a
124|fixed group of base holes. `finish` is `"plain"`, `"CB"` or `"CS"`, applied to
125|every hole of the mount (FLIGHT rule 2 applies). Offsets are from `origin`:
126|
127|| Name | Fastener | Holes (offsets from origin) |
128||------|----------|-----------------------------|
129|| PETREL-MOUNT-A | KF-M4 | (0,0), (40,0), (0,30), (40,30); origin = south-west hole |
130|| PETREL-MOUNT-B | KF-M5 | (0,0), (60,0), (0,40), (60,40); origin = south-west hole |
131|| STAR-TRACKER-3 | KF-M3 | 3 holes on a circle of diameter 30 about the origin, at 90°, 210°, 330° (0° = east, counter-clockwise) |
132|| HARNESS-P2 | KF-M2 | (0,0), (15,0); origin = west hole |
133|
134|A mount counts as one feature for `pattern()` (the whole mount is repeated)
135|and for `mirror()`.
136|
137|```python
138|p.mount("PETREL-MOUNT-A", origin=(10, 10), finish="CS")
139|```
140|
141|**pocket(at=(x, y), L, W, depth)** — a rectangular pocket cut from the top
142|face. (x, y) is the pocket's lower-left corner; `depth` must be less than the
143|stock thickness.
144|
145|```python
146|p.pocket(at=(10, 10), L=80, W=60, depth=4)
147|```
148|
149|**slot(at=(x1, y1), to=(x2, y2), width, depth="thru")** — a straight slot with
150|round ends along the centre line from start to end. `depth="thru"` cuts all the
151|way through; a number cuts a blind slot that deep from the top face.
152|
153|```python
154|p.slot(at=(10, 15), to=(40, 15), width=5)
155|```
156|
157|**pattern(nx, ny, dx, dy)** — repeats the LAST feature call in a grid, `nx`
158|by `ny` positions spaced `dx`, `dy` apart. The total is nx × ny instances
159|including the original call's position. Only boss, hole, pocket, slot and
160|mount can be patterned (a mount seed repeats the whole mount). After a
161|`mirror()`, `pattern()` raises a KeelError — there is nothing left to repeat.
162|(A leading text label, e.g. `pattern("hole", 2, 2, 48, 28)`, is accepted and
163|ignored.)
164|
165|```python
166|p.hole("KF-M4", at=(6, 6))
167|p.pattern(2, 2, 48, 28)
168|```
169|
170|**mirror(axis)** — copies every hole, boss, pocket, slot and mount recorded so
171|far to the mirror position: `axis="ew"` about the stock centre line x = L/2,
172|`axis="ns"` about y = W/2. Originals stay. Walls and wall holes are not
173|mirrored.
174|
175|```python
176|p.hole("KF-M5", at=(5, 5))
177|p.mirror("ew")   # second hole appears at (L-5, 5)
178|```
179|
180|**fillet(edges="vertical", r=None)** — rounds the stock's 4 vertical outer
181|edges. `r` defaults to your material's standard fillet. Only `edges="vertical"`
182|exists.
183|
184|```python
185|p.fillet()
186|```
187|
188|**finish()** — returns the part as exactly one solid. Must be the last call;
189|every program ends with `solid = p.finish()`.
190|
191|```python
192|solid = p.finish()
193|```
194|
195|**keel.render(p, path)** — writes an SVG preview of a finished part for the
196|dashboard catalogue. It needs a finished part, so call it after `finish()`.
197|
198|```python
199|keel.render(p, "brk_0101.svg")
200|```

203|
204|Keel errors are plain sentences starting with `keel:`. The common ones:
205|
206|- `keel: unknown fastener code 'M4'; holes use company codes KF-M2 ...` — you
207|  used a raw size instead of a KF code.
208|- `keel: stock() called twice; a part has exactly one base block ...` — delete
209|  the second `stock()`.
210|- `keel: hole() called before stock(); every part starts with p.stock(L, W, T)`
211|  — `stock()` must be the first call.
212|- `keel: unknown edge 'top'; edges are named 'north', 'south', 'east' or 'west'`.
213|- `keel: pattern() with no previous feature; call a feature first`.
214|- `keel: render() before p.finish(); finish the part first ...`.
215|- `keel: unknown material 'AL7075'; materials are AL6061, TI6AL4V, SS316 ...`.
216|- `keel: wall thickness 1.0 is thinner than the AL6061 minimum wall 1.5 ...`.
217|- `keel: flight parts need -CB or -CS fasteners (KF-M4 at (6, 6))` — FLIGHT
218|  parts need counterbored or countersunk base holes.
219|- `keel: wall_hole() on the 'north' edge with no wall; ...` — add the wall first.
220|- `keel: wall_hole() takes a plain KF code without -CB/-CS, got ...`.
221|- `keel: unknown mount 'PETREL-MOUNT-C'; mounts are ...`.
222|- `keel: pattern() after mirror(); there is nothing to repeat ...`.
